body: The spec's engineering hygiene is real — the leakage controls (FR-004, SC-004), the refusal to impute missing pH, and the explicit ban on synthetic-data fallback are all commendable, more disciplined than most proposals of this shape. But the whole edifice rests on a data source I cannot verify exists in the form assumed. NIST-IR-8200 is cited here as if it were a queryable corrosion database with a REST API, complete with 429-handling requirements — yet the artifact never establishes that such an API exists, what its schema is, or whether it contains the joint distribution of composition + environment + corrosion potential. The spec is careful to halt if the data is insufficient, which is honest, but it treats the existence of the data as an assumption rather than a checkable fact, and the entire P1 story is downstream of that assumption. Three further problems. First, FR-019's Materials Project merge is incoherent with FR-002: Materials Project is a DFT thermodynamics repository with no notion of corrosion-potential measurements or NIST record IDs, so 'link them by record ID, ensuring no fuzzy matching' between these two sources is not a design choice but an impossibility — the two databases share no keys. Second, FR-021 makes R² > 0.6 a system MUST. That is mandating a research outcome; a spec can require that the pipeline *measure* and *report* R², but requiring a particular score guarantees either failure-by-design or quiet pressure toward leakage. Third, the Leave-One-Specific-Alloy-Out split (US-1, scenario 3) puts exactly one alloy grade in the test set; an R² computed on a single held-out group is dominated by that group's internal variance and is nearly meaningless as a generalization estimate — with ≥10 designations available, leave-one-*group*-out CV or repeated group splits would be the defensible choice, and the spec's own minimum of 10 designations makes the single-holdout design look arbitrary. Minor: the pH edge case defines the 'standard aqueous range' as 'the full spectrum of the pH scale,' which is circular and also wrong in practice — concentrated acids and bases routinely yield pH < 0 or > 14, so FR-016 will flag physically legitimate extreme-environment records into a diagnostic bin rather than the regression.
